title: Customer escalation playbook for intermittent cross-region traffic oscillation
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Customers have reported intermittent 502/504 spikes and request routing oscillations between regions for a subset of tenants on hosted and dedicated fleets. Traffic appears to ‘bounce’ between primary and standby regions over a 30–90s window, causing duplicated requests, KV cache divergence, and increased tail latency. This ticket captures a customer-facing escalation runbook, triage notes, temporary mitigation lanes, and a short-term fix plan targeting both hosted and dedicated deployment modes (VPC/private deployments included).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Clear triage steps documented and validated against a simulated tenant that reproduces oscillation.
2) Emergency mitigation (ephemeral fallback lanes + tenant sticky routing) can be executed by on-call within 15 minutes.
3) A targeted hotfix that reduces oscillation frequency by >= 90% in canary for affected tenants.
4) Customer comms template and PagerDuty play created.
5) Postmortem actions and long-term remediation tasks scheduled.
runbook_steps:
1) Initial triage: check global routing metrics (console -> Routing -> RegionHealth) and confirm tenant shard(s) showing oscillation.
2) Identify recent rollouts: check /releases and runtime-1.22 canary rollout logs (GH PRs in references).
3) If tenant impact is high, mark tenant as P0 and notify Sales/Customer Success.
4) Apply temporary sticky policy: curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing -d '{"sticky":true,"duration_s":900}' (use runbook token). This pins traffic to last-known-good region.
5) For Dedicated customers, coordinate with on-call infra to apply a network-level blackhole to the flapping standby to eliminate rehome loops if safe.
6) Start KV-consistency job: run kv-sync-tool snapshot --tenant {tenant_id} --region primary && kv-sync-tool apply --target region-standby. Monitor kv-sync-tool logs in /var/log/kv-sync/{tenant_id}.
7) If oscillation persists after sticky policy + kv-sync, trigger staged evacuation: shift 30% -> 60% -> 100% to standby using weighted routing gates in the console; observe p50/p99 and error budget.
8) Once stable, roll back sticky policy and run a targeted hotfix rollout with tracing enabled to validate root-cause before wider rollout.
investigation_notes:
- First observed 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC on tenants t-324 and t-910.
- Symptoms: repeated client-side retries + duplicated completion tokens.
- Key metrics: p99 latency increased from 180ms -> 1.2s during oscillation; request duplication rate ~0.6% for affected tenants.
- Hypothesis A: health-check flapping due to transient kernel-level packet loss on egress in region eu-west-2 causing our smart routing to prefer alternate region then re-prefer primary.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache eviction mismatch + concurrent rehome created a short window where requests routed to both regions until KV reconciliation completed.
- Quick checks run: region-health API, kube node conditions, XDS route dump, autoscaler logs. Evidence pointed to combined network flapping + a race in our tenancy rehome orchestration (race window ~20–50s).
- Captured packet drops on frontend egress host: /var/log/syslog entries and cloud provider network health; raised to infra team (see references).
mitigations_applied:
1) Applied sticky routing for affected tenants (2026-03-09 04:00 UTC).
2) Launched kv-sync snapshot/apply to reconcile evicted keys (completed 2026-03-09 04:12 UTC).
3) Put temporary capacity cushion: spin up warm standby instances in target region and mark tenant priority to avoid autoscaler-driven churn.
4) For one Dedicated customer on private network, negotiated brief window for region-level blackhole to break rehome loop (completed 2026-03-09 05:00 UTC).
rollout_plan:
Short-term (hotfix):
- Build: Add a guard in rehome-orchestrator to hold final cutover until KV-snapshot confirmation and 60s stabilization timer.
- Canary: rollout to 5% of traffic for affected tenants on runtime-1.22-canary fleet for 2h with tracing.
- Metrics to watch: rehome count per-tenant, request duplication rate, p99 latency, KV-sync duration.
Long-term:
- Add cross-region health hysteresis and concurrency locks in rehome-orchestrator.
- Add route smoothing with exponential backoff to avoid oscillating reroutes.
- Integrate router-level sticky tokens and enable per-tenant rollback windows.
rollback_plan:
If hotfix causes regressions:
1) Immediately pause rollout and shift canary traffic back to previous runtime tag.
2) Remove the guard if it's blocking legitimate rehomes (via feature flag).
3) If network-level changes were applied to dedicated/private customers, reverse blackhole and re-evaluate with infra.
4) Inform customers via escalation channel with timeline and next steps.
communication_templates:
Customer escalation email (short):
Subject: Incident update - intermittent cross-region request duplication affecting {tenant_name}
Hi {customer_contact},
We’re investigating intermittent cross-region request duplication and elevated tail latency that affected your tenant. Our initial mitigations (sticky routing and KV reconciliation) have stabilized traffic for most tenants. We’ve scheduled a targeted hotfix and will provide a canary start time. We expect a complete remediation within 24 hours.
Best,
Asha (Site Reliability)

PagerDuty/Ops post (internal):
- Impacted tenants: {list}
- Action: sticky routing applied, kv-sync started, hotfix PR #PR_NUMBER in runtime repo.
- Next: canary rollout at {time}, on-call: {assignee}, infra: {infra_oncall}

Slack template for customer-facing channel: """Pinned: We're actively mitigating intermittent cross-region routing oscillations. Temporary sticky routing is enabled. We'll post updates every 30 minutes."""
postmortem_actions:
1) Ship rehome-orchestrator guard and route-smoothing change in runtime-1.23.
2) Add egress network observability (BPF-based drop counters) to detect packet loss patterns earlier.
3) Create an automated chaos test that simulates transient egress loss across region pairs and validates no oscillation occurs.
4) Update onboarding docs for Dedicated customers on networking expectations and runbook steps.
5) Schedule customer follow-up calls and include timeline of remedial work in account review.
